draft.title: Belief systems and ideologies
card: a set of ideas about the meaning of life and how people should live. A religion such as Buddhism or Islam is one example.
a set of political or social ideas about how society should be organised. Liberalism and socialism are examples.
The two overlap. Both are shared ideas that shape what people value and how they act.
The difference is the focus. A belief system is mainly about meaning and how to live. An ideology is mainly about how society and power should work.
draft.remember: A belief system is about meaning and how to live. An ideology is about how society should be run.

a.q: Which of these is best described as an ideology?
opts: Socialism, with its ideas about how society should be run
Buddhism, with its teachings on how to live a good life
A family's tradition of sharing a meal on Sundays
A person's habit of reading the news each morning
a.why: Socialism is a set of political and social ideas about how society should be organised, so it is an ideology. Buddhism is the most tempting wrong option, but it is mainly a set of ideas about meaning and how to live, which makes it a belief system.
a.clue: Look for the set of ideas about how society should be organised.

b.q: Leila follows Islam, and it guides how she lives each day. She also supports liberalism in politics. Which statement describes her correctly?
opts: Islam is her belief system and liberalism is her ideology
Islam is her ideology and liberalism is her belief system
Both Islam and liberalism are her belief systems
Both Islam and liberalism are her ideologies
b.why: Islam is a set of ideas about meaning and how to live, so it is a belief system. Liberalism is a set of political ideas about how society should be organised, so it is an ideology. The two can overlap, but each has its own main focus.
b.clue: Match each set of ideas to its main focus: meaning, or how society is run.

a.best: Socialism, with its ideas about how society should be run

b.best: Islam is her belief system and liberalism is her ideology

problems.detail: The right option includes the card's definition of an ideology ('ideas about how society should be run'), and the clue repeats that same wording. A student can match the phrase without knowing what socialism is. Two of the distractors are habits rather than sets of ideas, so they are easy to rule out.

a.q: Which of these sets of ideas is best described as an ideology?
opts: Ideas on who should own land, factories and banks
Rules on daily prayer and which foods people may eat
Teachings on what happens to a person after death
Teachings on how to find inner peace and live well
a.why: Who should own land, factories and banks is a question about how society and power are organised, so ideas about it form an ideology. Rules on prayer and food are tempting because they guide how people act, but they are about how a person should live, which is the focus of a belief system.
a.clue: Which one is about society as a whole, not one person's life?
